newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil gains nearly $4.00 on higher futures.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil gains nearly $4.00 on higher futures.

text.p: NWE gas oil was almost $4.00 stronger on Tuesday as futures dragged outright prices higher.
August IPE gas oil closed $3.75 up at $176.00 a tonne in a bounce higher that reflected Brent's hike late on Monday.
Dealers said differentials were unchanged in what many characterised as a slow market.
High prices and the current dollar mark exchange rate was crimping liquidity, dealers said.
Heating oil barges were attracting premiums only narrowly firmer with Rotterdam refinery material pegged between +50-75 cents on the buyer's side against +$1.00-$1.50 from the sellers.
EN590 barge differentials were about 50 cents stronger at $4.50-5.50.
Diesel cargo premiums were steady at around +$4.50 cif for 20-30 dates, pretty much in line with yesterday's deal of $4.45 against September.
There was some talk of EN590 getting a touch tight, but this was not reflected in stronger prices.

Russian gas oil was fairly well supplied, but exports should tail off as refinery maintenance kicks in. A couple of large 40,000 tonne parcels are heading into NWE helping to keep premiums no higher than +$1.00 cif.
DIN was attracting more interest than FOD and 10,000 tonnes was sold at $1.25 cif over September.
